This action supports the Committee’s view that sustained expansion of economic activity, strong labor market conditions, and inflation near the 2 percent objective are the most likely outcomes, but with notable caveats from the literature: investment-led components drive much of cyclical volatility, so ongoing weakness in business fixed investment and exports can materially weigh on real GDP (investment function and business-cycle evidence). Empirical work on monetary policy transmission (e.g., Sims-style VARs and Friedman’s documentation of policy’s impact on output) suggests that lowering the policy rate and maintaining ample reserves via T-bill purchases and repo operations should ease money-market pressures and support interest-sensitive spending. At the same time, with market- and survey-based inflation expectations low but stable, New Keynesian estimates of the Phillips curve (Galí, Gertler, and López-Salido) and inflation-targeting insights (Svensson) point to muted inflation pressures and a rationale for continued accommodation until inflation durably converges to target. Overall tone: modestly positive on growth support from policy, tempered by investment and trade headwinds and global uncertainty.
